pins.name: Stetattle Creek Trailhead, Diablo (approach; closed for post-fire hazards, check status)
pins.directions: Drive SR 20 to milepost 126 and turn into the town of Diablo (not Diablo Dam). The trailhead is just past the Stetattle Creek bridge at the entrance to town; park in the small turnout on the right, leaving room for others. Overnight stays need a North Cascades backcountry permit.

pins.name: Davis Peak summit
pins.directions: Hike the Stetattle Creek Trail about 2 miles, drop about 200 ft to ford the creek opposite Davis Peak, then bushwhack and scramble a Class 3-4 rib, roped for the slabby sections, through slide alder to flat ground at the toe of the glacier near 4,000 ft. Climb the glacier to the bergschrund, then the face and couloir to the summit ridge near 6,700 ft, and follow the ridge about an hour to the summit.

pins.name: Gorge Creek bridge, SR 20 (~MP 123) — descent exit and shuttle car
pins.directions: Descend the south ridge crest past the 5,720 ft saddle, over or around Point 5872, then straight down the trackless south-slope forest. The cliff bands near 2,800 and 2,400 ft must be turned on the right line, so do the top 1,500 ft in daylight and steer by compass to avoid drifting toward Stetattle Creek. You reach SR 20 at the Gorge Creek bridge, about four road miles west of Diablo.
